paramDefinitions.label: Trend weight
paramDefinitions.hint: Share of composite score from trend analysis. ↑ Higher → only clear trends pass (fewer results) · ↓ Lower → sideways stocks qualify (more results)

paramDefinitions.label: Pullback weight
paramDefinitions.hint: Share of score from pullback quality. ↑ Higher → only clean, shallow pullbacks pass (fewer) · ↓ Lower → any pullback depth qualifies (more)

paramDefinitions.label: Trigger weight
paramDefinitions.hint: Share of score from momentum timing signals. ↑ Higher → only active buying pressure qualifies (fewer) · ↓ Lower → weaker signals still pass (more)

paramDefinitions.label: Event weight
paramDefinitions.hint: Share of score from catalyst proximity. ↑ Higher → upcoming events penalise more stocks (fewer) · ↓ Lower → events count for less (more)

paramDefinitions.label: Vol weight
paramDefinitions.hint: Share of score from IV conditions. ↑ Higher → only calm-IV stocks qualify (fewer) · ↓ Lower → high-IV stocks still pass (more)

paramDefinitions.label: Min stock score
paramDefinitions.hint: Stocks-mode scans only (the Options scan does not read it). Drops any name whose stock score is below this. At or below 35 it adds nothing: a score under 35 is already REJECT and dropped.

paramDefinitions.label: Trend method
paramDefinitions.hint: Algorithm for scoring trend strength. Additive = price + slope + ADX combined; Crossover = MA crossover signal; Relative Strength = return vs. benchmark index

paramDefinitions.label: MA type
paramDefinitions.hint: Moving average type. EMA reacts faster to recent price (more signals, more results); SMA is smoother (fewer, calmer signals)

paramDefinitions.label: Fast MA period
paramDefinitions.hint: Short-period MA that detects momentum change. ↑ Higher → fewer, slower crossover signals · ↓ Lower → more frequent but noisier signals

paramDefinitions.label: Slow MA period
paramDefinitions.hint: Long-period MA representing the primary trend. ↑ Higher → stronger trend required (fewer results) · ↓ Lower → shallower trends qualify (more)

paramDefinitions.label: MA type
paramDefinitions.hint: Moving average type for the additive model. EMA → faster reaction (more results); SMA → smoother baseline (fewer results)

paramDefinitions.label: MA period
paramDefinitions.hint: Period of the trend-defining MA. ↑ Higher → longer trend baseline required (fewer) · ↓ Lower → more stocks qualify (more)

paramDefinitions.label: Slope lookback
paramDefinitions.hint: Bars used to measure MA angle (steepness). ↑ Higher → smoother reading, misses early moves · ↓ Lower → reacts faster but noisier

paramDefinitions.label: ADX period
paramDefinitions.hint: Bars for the Average Directional Index. ↑ Higher → smoother but slower ADX · ↓ Lower → quicker but noisier

paramDefinitions.label: ADX pass threshold
paramDefinitions.hint: Minimum ADX value for a PASS score. ↑ Higher → only strong trends qualify (fewer) · ↓ Lower → weak trends also pass (more)

paramDefinitions.label: ADX caution threshold
paramDefinitions.hint: ADX below this triggers CAUTION. ↑ Higher → broader caution zone, fewer clean passes · ↓ Lower → narrower caution zone, more passes

paramDefinitions.label: Price factor max pts
paramDefinitions.hint: Max points the price-above-MA check can contribute. ↑ Higher → price position dominates the trend score · ↓ Lower → price position matters less

paramDefinitions.label: Slope factor max pts
paramDefinitions.hint: Max points MA steepness can contribute. ↑ Higher → trend angle matters more · ↓ Lower → slope carries less weight

paramDefinitions.label: ADX factor max pts
paramDefinitions.hint: Max points ADX strength can contribute. ↑ Higher → directional strength required · ↓ Lower → ADX matters less

paramDefinitions.label: RS period
paramDefinitions.hint: Days of return used for benchmark comparison. ↑ Higher → structural outperformance required · ↓ Lower → recent momentum only

paramDefinitions.label: RS pass threshold
paramDefinitions.hint: Minimum return vs. benchmark for PASS. ↑ Higher → only clear outperformers qualify (fewer) · ↓ Lower → slight outperformers qualify (more)

paramDefinitions.label: RS caution threshold
paramDefinitions.hint: Return below this triggers CAUTION. ↑ Higher → stricter caution zone · ↓ Lower → slight underperformers still score cleanly

paramDefinitions.label: Benchmark index
paramDefinitions.hint: Index used as the return baseline. NDX = tech-heavy comparison; SPX = broad market comparison

paramDefinitions.label: RSI period
paramDefinitions.hint: Bars used to compute RSI. Set in the Trigger group (display only here).

paramDefinitions.label: Swing high lookback
paramDefinitions.hint: How many bars back to find the most recent swing high. ↑ Higher → broader context, fewer stocks qualify as pulling back · ↓ Lower → recent highs only (more)

paramDefinitions.label: ATR caution max
paramDefinitions.hint: Max ATR multiples a move can extend before CAUTION. ↑ Higher → extended moves allowed (more results) · ↓ Lower → only tight pullbacks pass (fewer)

paramDefinitions.label: Require reversal candle
paramDefinitions.hint: Requires a bullish reversal bar at the pullback low (e.g. hammer). On → fewer, higher-conviction entries · Off → all pullbacks qualify

paramDefinitions.label: MACD fast
paramDefinitions.hint: Fast EMA period in MACD. ↑ Higher → fewer, stronger signals · ↓ Lower → more frequent but noisier signals

paramDefinitions.label: MACD slow
paramDefinitions.hint: Slow EMA period in MACD. ↑ Higher → more pronounced divergence required (fewer) · ↓ Lower → smaller divergences trigger (more)

paramDefinitions.label: MACD signal
paramDefinitions.hint: Smoothing on the MACD histogram. ↑ Higher → slower, steadier confirmation · ↓ Lower → noisier, faster trigger

paramDefinitions.label: RSI floor
paramDefinitions.hint: Minimum RSI to confirm momentum is recovering at entry. ↑ Higher → only stocks with active buying qualify (fewer) · ↓ Lower → oversold stocks also pass (more)

paramDefinitions.label: Volume lookback
paramDefinitions.hint: Days used to compute the average volume baseline (display only).

paramDefinitions.label: Volume multiplier
paramDefinitions.hint: Required volume as a multiple of average on the signal day (display only).

paramDefinitions.label: Event reject days
paramDefinitions.hint: Stocks with a catalyst within this window are hard-rejected. ↑ Higher → wider safety zone (fewer) · ↓ Lower → closer-to-event entries allowed (more)

paramDefinitions.label: Event caution days
paramDefinitions.hint: Stocks within this wider window get a CAUTION flag instead of reject. ↑ Higher → larger amber zone · ↓ Lower → smaller amber zone

paramDefinitions.label: IV pass max (absolute)
paramDefinitions.hint: Max ABSOLUTE implied volatility (0–100%) for a PASS. This is the one that applies on most chains — a true IV rank needs IBKR or tastytrade to answer, and otherwise the contract carries a raw IV instead. N/A on Intraday. ↑ Higher → elevated-IV contracts still qualify (more) · ↓ Lower → only calm-IV contracts pass (fewer).

paramDefinitions.label: IV rank pass max (percentile)
paramDefinitions.hint: Max IV RANK — where today’s IV sits in the name’s own 52-week range (0–100) — for a PASS. Applies ONLY when IBKR or tastytrade supplied a real rank; otherwise the absolute ceiling above is what judges the contract. N/A on Intraday. ↑ Higher → elevated-IV stocks still qualify (more) · ↓ Lower → only calm-IV stocks pass (fewer).

paramDefinitions.label: IV rank lookback
paramDefinitions.hint: Lookback window used to normalise current IV into a percentile rank (display only).

paramDefinitions.label: HV period
paramDefinitions.hint: Days used to calculate historical (realised) volatility (display only).

paramDefinitions.label: Confidence caution below
paramDefinitions.hint: Signal backtest win rate below this % triggers CAUTION. ↑ Higher → broader caution zone · ↓ Lower → narrower caution zone

paramDefinitions.label: Confidence reject below
paramDefinitions.hint: Signal backtest win rate below this % triggers REJECT. ↑ Higher → stricter gate, better-tested results (fewer) · ↓ Lower → looser gate (more)

paramDefinitions.label: Confidence ATR target
paramDefinitions.hint: Win barrier for the mini backtest = this × ATR, for the active horizon. Overrides the Settings default for this scan only. ↑ Higher → demands a bigger winner (stricter, fewer)

paramDefinitions.label: Confidence ATR stop
paramDefinitions.hint: Loss barrier for the mini backtest = this × ATR, for the active horizon. Overrides the Settings default for this scan only. A lone target or stop override (without the other) is ignored.

paramDefinitions.label: Max delta
paramDefinitions.hint: Highest delta (0–1) allowed — controls how far in-the-money contracts can be. ↑ Higher → near-the-money contracts allowed (more) · ↓ Lower → OTM-only (fewer)

paramDefinitions.label: Bid-ask spread ceiling
paramDefinitions.hint: Max spread as a fraction of mid price. ↑ Higher → illiquid contracts included (more, but costly) · ↓ Lower → tight spread required (fewer, cheaper to trade)

paramDefinitions.label: Min option volume (0 = off)
paramDefinitions.hint: Optional hard floor on contracts traded, off (0) by default because volume is scored softly under Preferred Liquidity below. The figure is session-to-date volume, so with a floor set, results change with the time of day. ↑ Higher → better liquidity required (fewer) · ↓ Lower → thin markets allowed (more). Hard floor only: a thinner contract still misses Preferred min volume / open interest below, and can still be rejected for a contract score below the caution band or for too many soft misses (the two Preferred liquidity floors together count as at most one), so lower those too.

paramDefinitions.label: Min open interest
paramDefinitions.hint: Minimum outstanding contracts. ↑ Higher → requires an established market (fewer) · ↓ Lower → new or low-traffic strikes included (more). Hard floor only: a thinner contract still misses Preferred min volume / open interest below, and can still be rejected for a contract score below the caution band or for too many soft misses (the two Preferred liquidity floors together count as at most one), so lower those too.

paramDefinitions.label: Min delta (far OTM)
paramDefinitions.hint: Rejects contracts too far out of the money. ↑ Higher → keeps contracts closer to the money · ↓ Lower → very cheap deep-OTM contracts included

paramDefinitions.label: Min DTE
paramDefinitions.hint: Derived from the holding horizon (hold × 2). Change the horizon to change this.

paramDefinitions.label: Max DTE
paramDefinitions.hint: Derived from the holding horizon (hold × 2). Change the horizon to change this.

paramDefinitions.label: Preferred min volume
paramDefinitions.hint: Daily contract volume below this docks the liquidity score and together with Preferred min open interest counts as at most one soft miss. ↑ Higher → more contracts soft-flagged (fewer survive 3 misses) · ↓ Lower → fewer soft-flagged. Default: 200. Independent of the hard "Min option volume" floor above, an optional floor (off, 0, by default) which rejects outright rather than scoring.

paramDefinitions.label: Preferred min open interest
paramDefinitions.hint: Open interest below this docks the liquidity score and together with Preferred min volume counts as at most one soft miss. ↑ Higher → more contracts soft-flagged · ↓ Lower → fewer soft-flagged. Default: 1000. Independent of the hard "Min open interest" floor above.

paramDefinitions.label: Preferred spread ceiling
paramDefinitions.hint: Spread (as a fraction of mid) above this docks the spread score and counts as one soft miss. ↑ Higher → wider spreads tolerated before scoring/rejecting on this axis · ↓ Lower → stricter. Default: 0.08. Independent of the hard "Bid-ask spread ceiling" above, which is far looser (0.20) by default — this preferred ceiling is usually the tighter, binding constraint in practice.

paramDefinitions.label: Headwind caution %
paramDefinitions.hint: Sector underperformance vs benchmark below this % → CAUTION on candidate. ↑ Higher (closer to 0) → stricter, more candidates caught (fewer pass) · ↓ Lower → only severe laggards affected (more pass). Default: -15%

paramDefinitions.label: Headwind reject %
paramDefinitions.hint: Sector underperformance below this % → hard REJECT regardless of score. ↑ Higher (less negative) → stricter, more rejections · ↓ Lower → only catastrophic laggards rejected (more pass). Default: -40%

paramDefinitions.label: Fundamentals caution above
paramDefinitions.hint: BEARISH SCANS ONLY. Fundamental health score above this → CAUTION. Flags risk of shorting a financially strong company. ↑ Higher → only very strong companies flagged (fewer cautions) · ↓ Lower → wider caution zone (more cautions). Default: 70

paramDefinitions.label: Fundamentals reject above
paramDefinitions.hint: BEARISH SCANS ONLY. Fundamental health score above this → hard REJECT. Company is too financially strong to short safely. ↑ Higher → only fortress-balance-sheet companies rejected (fewer) · ↓ Lower → stricter, more rejections. Default: 80

paramDefinitions.label: Spread tolerance
paramDefinitions.hint: Max bid-ask spread as a fraction of mid price at entry. ↑ Higher → wider spreads allowed (more contracts, worse fills) · ↓ Lower → tight spread required (fewer contracts, better fills). Default: 0.10

paramDefinitions.label: Max slippage
paramDefinitions.hint: Expected slippage as a fraction of price. ↑ Higher → accepts poor fills (more, but costlier) · ↓ Lower → only clean-fill entries pass (fewer). Default: 0.03

paramDefinitions.label: Min premium
paramDefinitions.hint: Minimum option premium per contract in $. ↑ Higher → rejects cheap, illiquid options (fewer) · ↓ Lower → penny options included (more, but harder to exit). Default: $0.10

paramDefinitions.label: Target (R-multiple)
paramDefinitions.hint: First target distance in multiples of the stock-stop distance, with nearby structure preferred. Default: 2R

paramDefinitions.label: Bullish stop %
paramDefinitions.hint: Stop-loss distance for bullish trades. ↑ Higher → wider stop (more room, worse R/R) · ↓ Lower → tighter stop (better R/R but more stop-outs). Default: 3%

paramDefinitions.label: Bearish stop %
paramDefinitions.hint: Stop-loss distance for bearish trades. ↑ Higher → wider stop · ↓ Lower → tighter stop. Default: 3%
